entities.summary:
Guillem de Copons was a writer and diplomat of unknown Valencian origin, active in the 15th century.

He made significant translations of ancient Greek, classical Latin, and European Middle Ages literary works into Catalan, contributing to the preservation of these texts for future generations.

De Copons' translations had a lasting impact on the cultural landscape of the Mediterranean, influencing the development of Catalan literature and language.

The works he translated included those of the Roman poet Martial, whose satires continue to be studied for their wit and insight into human nature.

As a diplomat, de Copons played a crucial role in facilitating cultural exchange between the Mediterranean region and the wider world, fostering a spirit of cooperation and mutual understanding.

One notable example of his diplomatic efforts was his involvement in the negotiations leading to the Treaty of Tordesillas, which established the border between the Spanish and Portuguese empires in the Americas.

Through his work, de Copons helped to create a shared cultural heritage across the Mediterranean, promoting a sense of unity and shared human experience.

Guillem de Copons' legacy can be seen in the enduring influence of his translations on Catalan literature, as well as his role in shaping the cultural and diplomatic landscape of the Mediterranean.
